THE ROAD AHEAD

VOID Language roadmap.
A clear direction.

VOID is in active development. Here is what works, what is being improved and where the language is heading. No dates or completion percentages are promised.

Implemented foundationHosted verificationWork under verificationKnown limitsFuture direction
Implemented foundation

Programs, data and native execution

The compiler uses C++20 and LLVM/Clang/LLD 23.1.4. One lowering pipeline serves JIT execution and native object emission. Applications support main or top-level execution, file globals and ordered initialization. The numeric entry adapter remains available for small calculations.

Run and build an application

Verified on hosted systems

Compiler, Runtime and editor coverage

Compiler and Runtime suites have run on Ubuntu, Windows Server and macOS ARM64, including strict sanitizers on Ubuntu. VS Code integration runs against the real language server. The standard library includes math, random, collections, text encodings, binary streams, files, paths, OS queries and channels.

Browse all guides

Implemented · verification open

Networking and logging

HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, TLS verification, async DNS, uploads, redirects and streaming are implemented. Linux and macOS passed the hosted HTTP suites. Windows passed 340 of 341 tests in the relevant run. The remaining failure concerns explicit P12 client identity with Schannel. Logging has cross-platform functional coverage, while its performance review and release hold remain open after an unresolved optimizer incident.

Read about HTTP ownership · Logging

Known limits

Resources and interoperability

Runtime admission bounds network resources. Application-held response data and operating-system trust services have different memory costs. Native workers require supported value transfers. External native bindings require a trusted host. Clean-machine distribution and some editor combinations still need validation.

Native integration

Future direction

Packages and the development loop

Future work includes package discovery, broader typed native integration and a save-driven live workflow. Function-body replacement already exists in Runtime integration; automated watching and compatibility across arbitrary changes are separate goals. Public release timing is open.
